# omni_machine_wait (Resource)

Waits for a machine to register with Omni and connect, and records its UUID.

It is the bridge between whatever creates a machine, a VM on a hypervisor or a cloud instance, and the Omni resources that need the machine's UUID, such as `omni_machine_set_node`. Select the machine by `labels` when its UUID is not known in advance: give each machine a unique label through the `machine_labels` of `omni_machine_join_config`, and wait on that label here. Select it by `machine_id` when the UUID is known, for instance because it was set as the VM's SMBIOS UUID.

Only creating this resource waits. Refreshing it looks the machine up once and never blocks a plan: if the machine has gone from Omni the resource is planned for creation again, which waits for it anew. Destroying it leaves the machine registered unless `remove_on_destroy` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Omni names a machine by its UUID, which is not known until the machine has joined. Put a label
# unique to the machine into its join config: Omni signs it into the join token and copies it onto the
# machine when it registers, which is how to find the machine afterwards.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "worker_0" {
  machine_labels = {
    "terraform/machine" = "worker-0"
  }
}

resource "aws_instance" "worker_0" {
  ami           = data.aws_ami.talos.id
  instance_type = "m5.large"
  user_data     = data.omni_machine_join_config.worker_0.config
}

# Waits for the machine carrying the label to register and connect, and records its UUID.
resource "omni_machine_wait" "worker_0" {
  labels = {
    "terraform/machine" = "worker-0"
  }

  # A replaced instance is a new machine: wait for it again rather than keep the old UUID.
  triggers = {
    instance_id = aws_instance.worker_0.id
  }

  # The instance is destroyed together with this resource, so drop the machine from Omni as well.
  remove_on_destroy = true

  timeouts = {
    create = "20m"
  }
}

resource "omni_machine_set_node" "worker_0" {
  cluster     = omni_cluster.example.name
  machine_set = omni_machine_set.workers.id
  machine_id  = omni_machine_wait.worker_0.machine_id
}

# Where the UUID is known in advance, for instance because it was set as the VM's SMBIOS UUID, wait
# for it directly.
resource "omni_machine_wait" "known" {
  machine_id = "4c4c4544-0042-3510-8051-b4c04f4e4d32"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `labels` (Map of String) Wait for the one connected machine carrying all of these labels. Disconnected machines are not considered, so a machine left registered by a VM that has since been replaced does not get in the way of its replacement, which joins with the same labels. More than one connected match is an error rather than something to wait out, since it means the labels do not identify a machine. Mutually exclusive with `machine_id`.
- `machine_id` (String) The UUID of the machine. Set it to wait for a machine whose UUID is known; otherwise it is filled in with the UUID of the machine `labels` selected.
- `remove_on_destroy` (Boolean) Remove the machine from Omni when this resource is destroyed, as `omnictl cluster machine delete` or removing it in the UI does. Set it when the machine is torn down together with this resource, a VM destroyed in the same apply, so that Omni does not keep a disconnected machine around. A machine that boots again afterwards simply registers anew.

If the machine is still in a cluster, destroying first waits for Omni to take it out, which resets it, so it has to be running for that. Whatever runs the machine depends on this resource through `triggers` or `labels` and is destroyed after it, so the machine is only turned off once it has left the cluster. Turned off before, it would never be reset, and Omni would never finish removing it from the cluster.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that, when changed, make Terraform wait for the machine again. Pass the ID of the VM or instance backing the machine, so that replacing it waits for its replacement rather than reusing the UUID of the old one.

### Read-Only

- `connected` (Boolean) Whether the machine is connected to Omni. Always true right after the wait; a later refresh reports what Omni says at that time.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the machine, as a Go duration. Defaults to 15m0s.
- `delete` (String) With `remove_on_destroy`, how long to wait for the machine to leave its cluster before removing it anyway, as a Go duration. Defaults to 10m0s.
